1.Title: Nightmare's Emergence
1.Content:
Esperians are familiar with the name Ezizh, the demon that sows nightmares. But few know that the demon is only one apparition of many, while its true self burrows in the Twisted Realm, waiting for the opportunity to break into the reality. The Guardian of Dreams won't allow that, however. Tasi and her Dream Divers managed to trap Ezizh in the Twisted Realm, while its apparitions haunt dreams of mortals to keep it nourished.
    
    Now Ezizh is out of hibernation. With streams of power coursing through its body, it breaks free from the limbo, ready to claim the reality. It leaps from one nightmare to another, looking for the perfect foundation to build upon, to smother Esperia in desperation.
    
    Tasi, aware of the throbbing of nightmares, tried to thwart Ezizh's plan in dreams. But with Ezizh's elevated power, the best Tasi could do was to distract him. A game of cat and mouse began, through one dream after another, wonderous or grotesque.
    
    Just when Ezizh was about to capture Tasi, the duo stumbled into a horrendous nightmare, one where Esperia crumbles among disasters, vile creatures, and wars. It was the end of the world.
    
    Ezizh was thrilled. It was the most terrible nightmare that he was looking for. He left Tasi alone, shifting his attention to the dreamer instead. He must find the source of the nightmare and expand it into the reality.
    
    Tasi was terrified, because she knew the dreamer. Talene, the last successor of the Obsidian Finches. That reminds her of an unsettling rumor, that Celestials don't dream, unless it's an omen. This looks very much like an ill omen.
    
    But really, what does it mean?

2.Title: Winds of Change
2.Content:
In the Land of the Exiles, Thane endured the throbbing pain in his arm and swung his sword at the creature before him. Sweat and blood blurred his vision, and exhaustion was eroding his will, inch by inch. But he could not fall, for his best friend was behind him, and once he fell, Baden would be overwhelmed.
    
    During his journey with Talene and others in search of the Elemental Guardian, Thane encountered Baden in the Land of the Exiles. Baden and Respen suddenly found themselves surrounded by Corruptors. There was no time to catch up after years of separation. Thane and his party immediately joined the battle and fought side by side with Baden. Faced with a constant onslaught of Corruptors, the only way to survive is to eliminate the enemy.
    
    Despite the years of separation, they still understood each other as tacitly as they did on the battlefield back then, needing merely a glance for the other to comprehend their intentions. The pair attacked and defended methodically, breaking through the horde of Corruptors. Yet, as the circle shrank, the men were scattered by the surge of Corruptors, and Thane and Baden, the best of friends, became islands in a sea of aggression. The pair relied on each other to defend against the threats at their backs.
    
    Thane had no idea how many times he swung his sword, the corpses of the Corruptors piled high on the scorching yellow sand. Yet the Corruptors, like a frenzied ant colony, tirelessly lashed out their claws and teeth at the two men, and for every one that fell, there were still more monsters trampling over the bodies of their companions to fill the breach. They were exhausted from the fierce battle thus far, and could only force their numb bodies to hold on with the determination not to collapse. Through all endless killing, the duo had spent the last of their energy.
    
    Thane finally reached his limit, his body tottering, unable to fight against the advancing Corruptors. A spear with serrated teeth swept away the creatures around him, allowing Thane a brief respite. The only thing he saw through blurred vision was Baden holding off the Corruptors with his mangled frame, holding the spear across his chest and screaming for Thane to retreat.
    
    The look in Baden's eyes made Thane's heart burn, the expression in his best friend's eyes was as determined as when he died to save him, even though he knew the road ahead was dangerous, he was still ready to die. In that battle, he lost his arm, and his best friend lost his life trying to protect him. Now, the tragedy that he had regretted for half his life was about to repeat itself.
    
    Thane could not allow himself to watch his best friend die for him a second time. He resented his powerlessness, but he was too exhausted to grip his sword. Staring at his friend's back, Thane made a decisive stand. He sought the power of the Elemental Emblem from Respen, and although this would come at a great cost - becoming the Corruptors' target for the rest of his journey - he had no time to care about anything else. He was willing to pay any price if he could save his best friend.
    
    "I won't let this happen again!"
    
    The intangible winds converged in Thane's hands, the wind Wind Emblem fused with his body, and a surge of power rose up within him. Thane once again gripped the sword in his hand and swung with all his strength.
    A hurricane borne of the sword's tip, a blade of wind burst into the sky, and everything before him was enveloped in howling gusts. The sword blade broke free of the gale and furiously pierced the Corruptor in front of Baden.
    
    "This time, we fight side by side, together!"

3.Title: Chapter 1 Rising Winds
3.Content:
Ill omens first arose from feathered dreams
Warning Esperia of impending crisis
 
Among celebrations did such nightmares come to pass
 
As Rayne's female general fell with sickness
So a solitary one-armed soldier did set forth
 
In the Dark Forest fates mingled and merged
As divine bird and human warrior didst meet
 
The forest sage spoke freely of all things
And the truth behind disaster came to light
 
In the beginning,
Five elements together founded Esperia
 
Thus elemental imbalance creates catastrophe
And turns the world upside down
 
Only the combined power of the five Elemental Guardians
Can restore elemental order and avert disaster
 
Above golden sands they meet once more
The undead knight is surrounded on all sides
 
Wind's blessing of the swordsman grants tremendous might
And thus begins a new chapter in our tale

4.Title: Desperation
4.Content:
1. The Record Keeper
    My name is Albel. My grandfather is a church historian responsible for compiling records for the Lightbearer Temple. It's been over 40 years since we saw the end of the Hypogean War.
    Gods and Ancestors of every faction sacrificed much in exchange for that peace. Recording the glorious deeds of these heroes is my grandfather's job. According to him, those that achieve great things shine like brilliant stars, forever glimmering in the night sky of history.
    I once helped my grandfather sort out some of the historical data, and it was then that I discovered an omission from the history books.
    "... The 61st year of the Lightbearer calendar, winter. The war between Humanity and Hypogean has been going on for over 30 years. Despite the aid of other factions, the suppression of the Hypogeans has been too much for Humanity, and they show no sign of recovery. To save Esperia, the Goddess Dura created a huge anomalous space between dimensions that would be used to seal away the Hypogean...
    The Lightbearer's founding Emperor, Ancelot, lead his army and the armies of every faction united, driving the Hypogeans to the foot of the mountains, where Dura then opened the Barred Gate and managed to seal away most of the Hypogeans."
    Those words were the words of my Grandfather when he recorded the heroics events of that war more than 40 years ago. Yet, there is one pivotal name that has not been included, and who was absolutely vital to the campaign against the Hypogeans - The God of Thunder, Zaphrael.
    His deeds and words seem to have been entirely omitted, his existence deliberately erased from this legendary battle.
    It is impossible to put down to mere oversight. After grandfather passed away, I took some time to travel and tried piecing together Zaphrael's story from all kinds of sources, but despite everything I came up empty handed.
    I decided to visit my grandfather's old colleagues in the clergy and fellow historians, and they, too, kept silent on the matter. I believed I was going to live my whole life without ever finding the missing puzzle piece. That is, until I met them.
    I was in a small town at the westernmost edge of the Empire, beyond which was a barren wasteland.
    I briefly stayed in the town to see through the winter. That day, nightfall was approaching earlier than usual. Just as always, I played a few bars on my violin and hummed a few ditties, surrounded by the aroma of the inn's wines and seared meats.
    They're mostly tunes regaling stories of the greatness of Emperor Ancelot. Once that battle ended, his deeds became legend all throughout Esperia.
    Sat at the opposite table is a peculiar old traveler, the ends of his silver hair just peeking out of his hood. These small inns often have rooms for weary travelers in need of a night of rest, so at first I was totally oblivious to his presence.
    Until, that is, he bought me a drink and offered to tell me a story that I had never before heard.
2. Old Travelers' Tale
    It was a story about Zaphrael.
    Over 40 years ago, the allied forced, lead by Ancelot, faced with a brutal attack from the Hypogean forces. Seeing the Allies and the Hypogeans were fully engaged in combat, one particularly strong Hypogean snuck behind the lines and into the Allied base - Wardhurst Stronghold.
    "The garrison took a serious hit, even Bishop Hind was killed... Once Wardhurst Stronghold fell, rumors about Zaphrael and a Hypogean began to spread like an unbidden disease."
    The loss of Wardhurst Stronghold is certainly recorded in the historical records, but I knew nothing about any rumors.
    "What kind of rumors?"
    The candle on the travelers table dimmed momentarily, a single tear of hot wax dripping slowly downwards.
    "... Zaphrael let a Hypogean escape."
    Hearing this, I felt some doubts. According to the records, Zaphrael was the most impartial and stoic of all the Gods, how could he possibly have allowed a Hypogean to go free?
    Despite my concerns, I keep listening, not daring to interrupt.
    With the spread of the rumors, so too spread the distrust in Zaphrael, with a few particularly radical people even accusing him of failing to be worthy of his godhood, accusing him of causing the fall of the Stronghold.
    "No-one knows how the rumors came to be... but they served their purpose. The Allied forces are no more, and people doubt the oracles."
    "Once a flame of doubt has been lit, it is difficult to extinguish. Yet, from start to end, Emperor Ancelot believed in Zaphrael, even when his own 12 year old son, Marche, was lost during the Stronghold's fall.
    "The Hypogean responsible for the attack on the Stronghold, she knew everything there was to know about him, and she used it to her advantage." The traveler fell silent for long while.
    There's no mention of anything like this Hypogean in the records of the fall of Wardhurst Stronghold, it doesn't exist. Who on earth is this Hypogean? I unconsciously sat up and leaned in ever so slightly. Even though the traveler had only just begun telling the story, I was already deeply invested.
    "Then came the final battle of Bitter Rift. This was the final step of the Allied forces plan, Goddess Dura would seal the Hypogeans away by dragging them into Bitter Rift. In order to pull this off, Ancelot used himself as bait, luring the Hypogeans into the Rift."
    It was horrific battle. The blood of hundreds of elite guards stained the white snow of the Rift crimson red, the wind and snow whirled with Hypogean roars as they tore humans limb from limb and trampled their bodies and armor into the blood-soaked mud. Overwhelmingly powerful, the Hypogean forces blocked off every exit, ensuring retreat was impossible for Ancelot and his unit.
    Ancelot was down to his final two guards, when Goddess Dura finally succeeded in opening the Barred Gate, and Zaphrael leapt into Bitter Rift to reinforce and save Ancelot.
    "Ancelot had intended to sacrifice himself for the sake of humanity, but perhaps in Zaphrael's eyes, Ancelot represented new hope for the human Empire."
    With Zaphrael's appearance, so too appeared that same nightmarish, garrison wrecking Hypogean. This time, she came for Ancelot.
    She lunged towards Ancelot like a streak of pure evil, and despite Zaphrael's counterattack, she still takes Ancelot down.
    I had heard long ago that Ancelot was a soldier his entire life, and that he had lost his left eye during the Hypogean war, but I had never imagined such a terrifying plight.
    The old man continued his story. The temporal anomaly at Bitter Rift is already beginning to burst as the Barred Gate pulls in Hypogeans. Zaphrael and this Hypogean demoness fight near the Gate's edge, golden lightning arcs roaring over the Rift as the Hypogean cleave through the storm clouds one after another.
    "You should've come after me," Zaphrael lamented, his usually solemn voice tinged with sadness, "Marche... He was just a child..."
    "And what about Owain!?" The Hypogean's face contorts with rage, her sword slicing through a bolt of lightning, her eyes flickering with malice.
    It was a ruthless fight. With both the Thunder wielding God and the Hypogean wielding the Dark Star wishing death upon each other, doing all in their might to exert lethal force enough to end the other.
    However, Hypogeans are no match for the Gods. Finally, she is seriously injured and kneels at the cusp of the Barred Gate. Zaphrael faces her, the long spear of a hunter forms in his hand. All he has to do it throw it with all his might, and the Hypogeans life will be extinguished. Yet, he can't help hesitating.
    The two minds at work inside the Hypogean see their chance, goading and mocking him in an effort to shake his determination.
    "God of Thunder, take a look... Do you see what you've done to her? What monster she has become? Is that your justice?"
    "I'm sorry about Owain." Zaphrael ignored the taunting, looking straight into the Hypogeans hate-filled eyes. His usually dignified tone was now low and hoarse, "If I had to do it again, I would... But this time, Lucretia, there's no justice... We have been trapped by our mistakes... And this mistake has to end, but... I will end it with you."
    The bolt in Zaphrael's hand dimmed, his mind seemingly made up. He took a final look back at Ancelot, bidding his last farewell. Suddenly, he charged at the Hypogean, allowing her blade to pierce his shoulder as he hugged her tightly, pulling her down with him into the Barred Gate, both pulled into the vortex's core.
    At this very moment, the energy flow of the Oblivion Gate exploded, swallowing the entire Bitter Rift in the blink of an eye.
    ...
    After hearing his whole tale, I couldn't unwind for a long time. I had some thoughts and conjectures, but I was still confused by the whole thing. "According to you, if Zaphrael hadn't come, Ancelot would've died in Bitter Rift, so why on earth would such important deeds of heroism be swept away?"
    The traveler said nothing, but I followed his eyes and look over to the folks praying piously. The Lightbearer Temple's reputation has peaked in these last few decades, and every corner of the Empire feels it's influence, so even here in this tiny town, there are devotees.
    "Your songs are beautiful." The traveler said a little absent-mindedly. "And Zaphrael... He was the most devoted disciple I've ever seen. He did what he had to do, and that should never be forgotten... It's just, the Sanctum is like a pure white light, and they don't want it to be dirtied. As a God, he cannot just shirk his responsibility and let her walk away... Because that Hypogean woman, Lucretia, is not just anyone. She was once Zaphrael's wife."
    The candle has burnt out, the traveler has drunk his wine.
    He drops two copper coins on the table and gets up to leave. "Wait a moment!"A question suddenly dawned on me, "How do you know so much about a situation that only Ancelot and his two last bodyguards could've seen?"
    The old man stayed silent, walking to the door of the inn. His back was as a straight as blade sheathed after a long battle.
    As the door was slowly opened, a beam of morning sunshine came through. That beam of light illuminated the face under the travelers hood. A face with sharp edges and a wise, unshakable resolve. However, the most striking detail was surely the deep scar etched into his left cheek, crossing his left eye.
    
4. Future Generations
    The stories of heroes live on in immortality, but alas, mortals grow old.
    My time is short, and I can feel my life ebbing away from my body. As my body aged, it hasn't been so easy to travel. After thinking about it for a long time, I decided once I put pen to paper, that I should make a record of Zaphrael's story.
    If even one person sees it, I will consider myself fortunate. No matter whether or not history tries to silence them, some people will always shine like bright stars in the night sky of history.

5.Title: A Flame Reborn
5.Content:
Talene, the last surviving bloodline of the Obsidian Finch species. Her flame flickers and wavers deep within the dark depths of the forest, meanwhile a thick, icy haze slowly devours what little light remains in the forest, threatening to completely snuff it out. Before her, a ferocious purplish-red flame rages wildly, as if wanting to devour all in its path. The manifestation of a nefarious, grinning demon has appeared within the flame. It was this very kind of flame that had previously made Talene lose all hope as a youngling. Despair once again looms closer.
    
    "Talene... Talene... Hurry, wake up..."
    While in a trance, Talene could seemingly hear her mother's distant call. In the deepest reaches of her memory, it was there she found her. A manifestation of her mother appeared before Talene's own eyes, enveloped by blazing, demonic flames. Talene reached out to grasp her mother, but after a few short seconds she would watch her fade into the ether. With a furrowed brow and trembling arms, Talene struggles with her inner turmoil, struggling in vain to wake herself from the deep memories that entrance her. That ominous flame draws closer...
    
    "Talene... Astar will protect you..."
    Dazed, Talene sees yet another scene unfurl before her. Astar looked back worryingly at Talene as she steeled her resolve, and with a look of determination on her face, dove into the sea of fire.
    
    Talene could not allow herself to sink into despair again. Both her eyes flickered open, a pure fire burning fiercely within them as she burst upward out of the forest. Golden embers flitted in her wake, piercing the enveloping darkness! The Solaris Flare can never be extinguished and shall forever continue to burn. Its pure fire can be rekindled from its fallen embers. The Obsidian Finch soars toward Esperia in a new form, a new legend is about to be written.

6.Title: The Anguished
6.Content:
It was just as my dreams had foretold. The temple where the tormented goddess was being held lay at the foot of the mountain range. I stood where the setting sun could be seen, shining through a crevice, and observed the unfolding scene.
    —Rather than call it a temple, perhaps it's better to describe it as a tower without doors.
    I recalled my dreams, depicting the scene within the temple: the divine goddess shackled to the wall by the Hypogean, sharp spikes driven through her wings, horrifying streaks of blood.
    She told me of her agony, that her name was Vyloris, and that she had been deceived into leaving the safety of her mountain top and descending unto this place of pain. Bewitched and beguiled by the Hypogean, her captors have since tortured and tormented her without end, all to drain every drop of divine power from her.
    In my dream, I swore that I would save her before darkness enveloped all. I would defeat the Hypogean holding her captive, and deliver her from suffering.
 
    Under the brilliance of a rising full moon I found the loathsome Hypogean, drew my weapon and attacked. No expression could be discerned on the fiend's foul, mangled face, but he clearly hesitated—as if he wished to speak.
    A repugnant whooshing noise came from his throat. I understand not the Hypogean language, nor did I want my determination to be undermined, so I raised again my sword and struck fiercely.
    The outcome of our mortal fight was uncertain, but victory ultimately fell to me. It was with the purest joy that I plunged my blade deep into the beast's chest. The bright red blood which spurted from his fatal wound seemed identical to mine.
    Right then, I was so tired I felt like I could barely stand.
    But I mustered the last of my strength to cleave in twain the wall to which the goddess was chained. I saw Vyloris break free from her bonds amidst the swirling dust. She smiled and walked toward me, and as she embraced me I knew that everything I had done was worth the effort.
    Just then, the gentle and caressing hand of the goddess on my chest transformed into a razor-sharp claw. Black light enveloped me, as every inch of both armor and flesh disintegrated under that terrible claw.
    It was soul-light, the light of the Infernal Surge.
 
    "What a just and handsome knight you are, just like the previous pitiful wretch... The one you just defeated." I screamed, eyes wide in fear and pain as I watched her slash my face and cut out my tongue with keen-edged blades. "I'd really hate to kill you. You don't foolishly think, like him, that chaining me up in a temple could possibly seal a demoness?"
    I looked at the limp figure on the ground, of the "Hypogean" I had just slaughtered. I tried to call for help, but nothing but a hideous whooshing noise emerged.
    I finally realized what he was trying to tell me. But I could only howl in frustration and regret—that mangled, hideous face was only so because of the inhuman torture inflicted upon it.
    Night fell, and I had not defeated the true Hypogean. All too soon, my eyesight was taken from me. I was left with but a poor sense of hearing as, accompanied by Vyloris' joyful humming, I fell into total darkness.
 
    "Lies are intoxicating, because people only believe what they want to believe."

7.Title: Chapter 2 Trials and Tribulations
7.Content:
Bound by duty, the heroes make tracks,
Traipsing through turbulent, riotous sands.

Earth Guardian, hidden though it stays, 
yet sits amidst a pair of duelists' fray. 

Mighty Lion sword bearer, contesting teacher turned betrayer,
Old versus young, Blood Claw grievances meet their slayer.

Once the curtain of the final act falls on the battlefield, 
the Chieftain, wise and knowing, does history's secrets now reveal. 

In time long past, Chief and Teacher did agree,
false enemy collusion to unify Mauler community.          

Lion sword bearer, by unspoken truth so deeply felt,
resolved to take up the torch, bare the flame himself.

Blade newly reborn, remolded by earth,
