8.Title: The Blood Claw-Legacy
8.Content:
Brandishing his lethal blade, Brutus dispatched his final foe into the dust. Grasping his greatsword with both hands, he listened to the scout's account of how a group of wicked monsters had recently appeared near the Mauler border. They were said to have appeared out of thin air, attacking the surrounding villages and gradually becoming a threat to Mauler stability itself.
    "One more thing... That person you've been looking for was spotted in the Weatherworn Dunes."
    Brutus kept a neutral expression in the face of this unexpected news, but his eyes betrayed a glimmer of excitement.
    "Found you, Anasta."
    
    The Weatherworn Dunes lies deep within the Scorched Expanse. In this uninhabited stretch of desert, which no one rashly enters, apparently tranquil dunes conceal the lethal quicksand underneath. Yet now, on the dunes above, Brutus is locked in vicious combat, his opponent wielding a sword the height of a man. Heavy blows send sand flying as the warriors' two weapons clash again and again in the fierce desert heat.
    "I've been looking for you a long time, you Mauler traitor."
    Brutus faces none other than Anasta, his one-time mentor and former Blood Claw, she who had betrayed the Maulers before fleeing.
    It seems like so long ago now, when Brutus had inadvertently discovered proof of Anasta's collusion with the Lightbearer nobility, and led his followers to foil her plot to seize the position of the Wise One. Once the dust had settled, the various tribal chieftains, realizing that humans were their common enemy, unanimously selected Skriath as their Wise One. Under his leadership, the Maulers set forth upon a unified path, with Brutus as the Blood Claw. While still highly respected among the Maulers, the stain of Anasta's treachery undoubtedly still sullied the name of Blood Claw.
    Brutus was troubled that the name inherited from a traitor had lost its due glory. He had never fully accepted the title even within his own heart, and the historical Blood Claw cloak and crown were sealed deep within the temple and never worn.
    The traitor Anasta had disappeared, reviled and hated by all the Maulers. Yet throughout all the years, Brutus had never given up the hope of tracking down his one-time mentor. Now, today, he finally gazed once more upon her as she stood before him in the flesh.
    Even after so many years it was an oddly familiar feeling to fight with Anasta once again. While he had never before managed to best her in the past, today he was a different caliber fighter. After clashing together again and again, Brutus caught her off-balance and sent her weapon flying, before knocking her to the ground.
    Brutus advanced, his vicious blade pointed at Anasta's neck, yet did not strike. "You were never so ambitious and hungry for power. Why did you betray us? Why?!!" Anasta had no intention of replying, wishing only that he do what must be done to finish this battle.
    "TELL ME THE TRUTH!" Defeating his mentor had never been Brutus' ultimate aim. For years he had harbored suspicions about her betrayal and right now, right here, he needed to know the truth.
    "Then allow me to enlighten you..." Skriath's distant voice came to Brutus' ears as his figure slowly emerged from within the whirling, dancing sand, "...about what really happened." 
    
    The Maulers had been divided ever since the assassination of the previous Wise One. The Lightbearers had seen an opportunity to continue destabilizing the Maulers, and secretly funded the Quicksand Claws to provoke internal conflict between the tribes. The tribal leaders, for their part, were totally unaware that their strings were being pulled. They acted just as expected, tearing each other apart while the humans reaped the benefit.
    Skriath and Anasta were rare visionaries among the Maulers. They astutely identified the real reason for the fracturing of Mauler society and, after contacting each other, the two kindred spirits quickly decided to cooperate with each other.
    The two wise Maulers fully understood that the current internal strife and divisions were preventing any hope of Mauler unification, and that intestine bellicosity would do nothing but bog down the Maulers in interminable conflict. Even if they declared unity to the outside world, this would be superficial only, as the individual tribal chieftains would never actually pledge loyalty to a unified force. These chieftains had only their own self-interest in mind and, as soon as an opportunity arose, would be sure to strike for their own gain. A common enemy was needed to truly end Mauler division and bind the tribes together in common enmity. It was evident that this common enemy had to be the Lightbearers, they who had been profiting from the internal discord of the Maulers, and that an opportunity had to be created to awaken those selfish chieftains to this reality.
    So the two of them acted at odds with one another, appearing to all observers as though they were contending for the leadership. In reality, however, they were secretly formulating a careful plan, and waiting for the right time to present itself.
    Soon enough, the Lightbearers sent word via the Quicksand Claws, promising Anasta power in exchange for eradicating the threat poised by Skriath. This was just the opportunity they had been waiting for, and decided to use supposed "treachery" to expose the Lightbearer plot. Crucial to the plan was a warrior of sufficient renown and loyalty to the Maulers, who could foil Anasta's "plot" before assuming the mantle of Blood Claw. In this way they could command their warriors to pledge allegiance to the Wise One.
    Brutus was just such a warrior.
    Brutus did not disappoint. Everything went according to plan, and the Maulers finally edged closer to unity. Anasta disappeared behind the scenes, as arranged by Skriath, until the Earth Guardian Granit was called upon by Skriath to assist in halting the spread of quicksand in the Weatherworn Dunes. Anasta was due to come too, to protect the Earth Guardian.
    
    Brutus was visibly moved by the truth, as the suspicions in his heart were at long last confirmed: This noble warrior in front of him had never truly betrayed her people. Brutus took a long, shuddering breath, while Anasta gazed upon her favored student before speaking slowly: "Sacrifices must be made, for Mauler unity... And when the tribe is in crisis, it falls to the Blood Claw to lead the way."
    Presently, Anasta looked to Skriath and inquired why he had come to the Weatherworn Dunes. He explained the purpose of his trip: the elemental imbalance was growing, and terrible creatures called Corruptors were rampaging, foreshadowing imminent catastrophe. Only Elemental Guardians could prevent such catastrophe but Granit was busy dealing with the quicksand and was unable to leave the desert. Crucially, some individuals were able to inherit the power of the Earth Emblem, and Skriath believed that Anasta was a prime candidate.
    And now Granit's voice rumbled from nearby: "There is a heavy price for accepting the Earth Emblem. The Emblem brings with it not just power, but unknown adversity. It represents a mortal attraction to all Corruptors, as the two are natural enemies and ceaselessly stalk each other. You will never know another second's true safety."
    Anasta did not hesitate, having long ago decided to give everything for her tribe. Just as she was about to accept her new role, Brutus strode forward. Standing in front of Granit he demanded, "Let me do this."
    Brutus knew that his mentor had already shouldered too much. He felt that now was the time to step up and take on her task and responsibility, no matter the price. He gazed resolutely at his mentor: "When the tribe is in crisis, it falls to the Blood Claw to lead the way."
    The Earth Emblem soared from Granit's body, and attached itself above Brutus' sword hilt. He is about to set foot on a new path but, before he begins, he still has one more thing to do.
    
    Brutus slowly emerges from the temple, whence he had just recovered the cloak and crown sealed within. Where once he had rejected these sacred items of the Blood Claw, now he will proudly complete his mission as the true Mauler Blood Claw.
    Outside the temple, a dense crowd of Corruptors had gathered, drawn by the Elemental Emblem. Faced with such a writhing mass of foes, Brutus grasps his weapon firmly and strides resolutely forward. He has eyes only for his enemy, while the sage words of his mentor echo in his heart:
    
    "Maulers, born from defiance.
    We possess an indomitable will that courses through our veins, and the Blood Claw is the absolute manifestation of this will.
    One day in the future, you shall inherit this will of ours, and become the Blood Claw.
    The road is fated to be difficult, surrounded by powerful enemies, outnumbered and alone.
    When the Tribe needs you, you must rise to the occasion.
    Your body a blade, carve your way forward!"
    
    Brutus' pace quickens as he rushes into the mass of Corruptors, his sharp blade felling them on all sides.

9.Title: Chapter 3 Dark Undercurrents
9.Content:
When the unbalanced elements envelop the forest
A shy girl meets a boy

The very trees cry out at the elemental chaos  
Together the two travel to the secret at the forest's heart  

Where the Elemental Emblem lies hidden in the Yuexi Spring
The treacherous boy attempts to seize it for himself

But before the Emblem is found, monsters attack
The boy repents with his life, so the girl can escape

But she cannot bear to abandon her former companion
Her loyalty elicits a response from a water element

Monsters retreat where the water flows
Her newfound powers will protect the forest's tranquility

10.Title: Chapter 4: Blight
10.Content:
On that forsaken Graveborn isle,
the scourge of elemental imbalance has descended.

The Elemental Guardian is held captive,
the wandering knight comes to rescue unattended.

They traveled through dark woods,
and encounter a monster with sharp claws.

With its unrelenting attacks,
the two could not escape without cause.

A flashing blade emerges out of nowhere.
The swordsman has arrived almost out of thin air.

Old friends reunite and fight back-to-back.
The knight and the swordsman join together and attack.

The power of the wood element flows into the knight.
The tide has turned, and the heroes deal a divine smite.

11.Title: Life Begins Anew
11.Content:
Baden evaded the swarms of Corruptors to make it to the very heart of the Island of the Banished. There, deep in the forest, vines twisted and knotted together to form a cage, in which a sleeping beauty could be glimpsed. Seeing that she was uninjured, Baden gave a sigh of relief before quietly calling her name. 
 
    "Nevanthi! Wake up!"
 
    The woman who slumbered amongst the trees was the Wood Guardian, Nevanthi, whom Baden had first encountered on the Island of the Banished many years ago. Back then, the solitary Baden had been wandering the length and breadth of Esperia, and happened upon the mysterious island. Suddenly confronted by Graveborn, Baden had readied himself for battle, but was severely weakened by a combination of years of travel, and the inescapable Graveborn curse. He found himself surrounded, before finally falling to the earth.
 
    As Baden came around, he heard a gentle voice by his ear: "Be still. Your Graveborn curse has not yet been fully contained." Before his eyes was a beautiful, delicate woman with a magical rune gleaming from her forehead. The potent breath of life effused from this rune, and followed her hands to brush over his bandaged body.
 
    "Those Graveborn..."
 
    "They are the Tainted, and they are as you: Graveborn who have lost their home."
 
    Seeing that Baden was now fully awake, Nevanthi moved to the side, revealing the Tainted clustered behind her. Their withered faces were beaming with smiles of welcome and friendship.
 
    "Welcome to the Island of the Banished, home of the Tainted."
 
    Accompanying Nevanthi allowed Baden to see the true nature of these denizens of the Island of the Banished. They were totally different from the impression Baden had of Graveborn and, while their features were terrifying, they were possessed of warmth and kindness. In his eyes these Tainted, with their hatred of immortality, were more akin to himself than either humans or the corrupted, fallen Graveborn.
 
    There was peace here equal to that of ordinary human villages, perhaps even more so, as the island avoided the conflicts and turmoil of the outside world.
 
    "You are welcome to stay here, should you so desire." Nevanthi invited Baden with a smile, and yet he did not immediately respond.
 
    "I see you still have someone special to miss. Who are they? Family? Lover? Friends?"
 
    "The closest, dearest friend of my entire life."
 
    Baden did not take up the invitation to settle on the island, but neither did he definitively rule it out. He kept drifting around Esperia, yet would often think of the lonely paradise that was the Island of the Banished, particularly when he quietly gazed out at his homeland from the Lightbearer border. His wanderings occasionally led him back to the island as a visitor, where he would share news of the mainland. He told himself that he visited for brief respite from his curse but, perhaps without even realizing it himself, he began to visit more and more often. 
 
    The day came, however, when Baden paid one of his occasional visits to the Island of the Banished, only to find it affected by Elemental Strife. A miasma of decay covered the entire island, the trees warped and ominous, as a swarm of Corruptors seethed forth from the forest to occupy the once paradise. Nevanthi expended almost all her power to protect the Tainted and fell fast asleep. Before succumbing to sleep, however, she had woven a cage of vines around herself, imprisoning herself in the hope of any eventual rescue.
 
    Baden had not lost his prudence, and realized that rash actions on his part would do nothing but endanger himself and doom the Island of the Banished. Thus he went first to the Dark Forest, where he sought the other Elemental Guardians to assist with the rescue. After meeting with the Wind Guardian, they sneaked back onto the Island of the Banished to execute the plan. The Wind Guardian had staged a diversion to attract the horde of Corruptors, and this allowed Baden, familiar as he was with the island's topography, to reach Nevanthi.
 
    Baden, the weak Nevanthi following, quickly but cautiously moved through the gloom of the forest. The Island of the Banished, once a paradise and refuge for the secluded Tainted, was now filled with scenes of devastation and disaster. Corruptors infest the warped woods, and a single misstep means being surrounded. But as long as they got through the forest to the coast, they would be able to escape the hunt by a departing ship prepared by Baden.
 
    "Don't worry. I will get you out of here."
 
    The elements are already in chaos... I've used too much power to suppress the corruption. Disaster is inevitable... You go find the other Elemental Guardians...
 
    "I'll never abandon a friend." Baden's voice is firm, as when he had saved Thane on the battlefield, "Nevanthi, just hold on. Reinforcements are coming."
 
    The Corruptors were like ants, infesting the woods and impossible to avoid. But Baden keenly sensing a gap in their ranks, broke through with Nevanthi, the Corruptors hot on their heels.
 
    "Reinforcements... You mean that friend you spoke of?"
 
    "We had an agreement. He was to join me here on the Island of the Banished, once the Earth Guardian was found."
 
    The Corruptors tripped and stumbled over the roots and vines which Nevanthi caused to erupt from the earth, but still new ones came, treading on the fallen forms of their fellows in their endless chase.
 
    Suddenly, an enormous monster appeared in the midst of the Corruptors. Its body was fashioned from withered, twisted branches, and the stench of decay filled the air around it. It was an aberration even among the Corruptors, and the source of the island's woes. Vines rotted and decayed in the monster's wake, turning the ground into a putrid bog. It was behind them in a flash, so close it seemed it could just reach out and grab them both.
 
    "I don't think we can wait for reinforcements. You must go, Baden!" Nevanthi despaired at their grim situation, but still she exhorted Baden to leave, saying that at least he could save himself. But Baden did not leave, choosing instead to turn and face the enemy.
 
    "Just hold on. As long as I am here, he WILL come."
 
    The huge monster towered above, looking down at the desperate, stubborn warrior who stood before it, already enveloped in the shadow of despair.
 
    Suddenly a sword of light came screaming down, driving back the huge Corruptor. The dazzling light faded, only to reveal Thane standing before Baden.
 
    Baden asked Nevanthi to retreat into the woods and recover her strength, while he rushed forward to help Thane. He knew that in his present weakened condition, he stood no chance in a direct clash with the monster. Therefore, he kept pace at the side, observing its movements and pointing out weaknesses to Thane.
 
    No match for the monster's strength, Baden and Thane work almost as one. With Baden's support, Thane gradually finds a good offensive rhythm, and is locked in battle with the huge Corruptor. The fight drags on, as Thane is unable to find a killing blow. Facing such a critical situation, Baden decides to take a risk to break the deadlock. He charges, brandishing his bone spear and sawblade, and lands a blow which staggers the giant Corruptor.
 
    Thane sees his opening and strikes, slashing a deep wound open on the monster's chest. However, the injury sends it into a frenzy and, ignoring Thane's blows, it instead charges at Baden, intent on crushing the annoying insect.
 
    Baden is sent flying by the enraged Corruptor. He smashes into the forest while Thane, distracted, is forced to yield ground.
 
    In the forest, Nevanthi braces herself and calls out to Baden. He was already covered in scars, and his constant struggles meant his body was always on the verge of total collapse. With the last of her strength, Nevanthi suspends the Elemental Emblem in the air before Baden. This was her final hope, but it comes at a very heavy cost.
 
    "Baden, my friend... I am powerless to restore your body. However, the Elemental Emblem offers you a chance to... change. If you take it, you are giving up your hard-won peace to become a target of the Corruptors..."
 
    Baden reaches out his hand and grasps the Wood Emblem. Its light totally envelops him, from which brilliance comes calm, resolute words:
 
    "I have only ever known peace in my dreams..."
 
    "It's my destiny to be chased by these shadows..."
 
    "However, I will never fight alone again!"
 
    Surrounded by light, Baden steps forward, his broken body made whole once more through the elemental power of the Wood Emblem. Ahead, Thane and the Corruptor are again locked in bitter battle, a battle which Baden now joins! Thane and he exchange a glance, their years of unspoken understanding rendering words unneeded. Fighting together once more, Thane's wind blades dance continuously, while Baden wields the power of the Wood Emblem to hinder the monster's movements with vines. 
 
    Thane sees his chance and, in a flash, cuts through the energy shield on the monster's chest, exposing a core which shimmers with elemental light. Baden takes over, striking the core with a spear of concentrated wood energy. It is a fatal blow. There's a sudden, violent explosion of energy, and the huge Corruptor falls to the ground with an earth-shaking crash.
 
 
    The battle has settled, and the immediate crisis has passed. But Baden cannot rest. Elemental Strife not only continues, but is getting progressively worse. The remote Island of the Banished will no longer stay untouched by the chaos.
 
    "Let's fight, Thane. Just like the old days."
 
    "Just like the old days."

12.Title: Chapter 5: Dawn of Hope
12.Content:
The young priestess prays reverently in the temple,
For the darkness to remain far from the Lightbearer Empire.

The dead lie still,
The Light finding no purchase.

The girl grasps for some other means to avert disaster,
Finding faint hope in tales of Elemental power.

Her mentor, devout in his belief in the Light, denies her entreaty.
Thus she travels. Alone, far from home, looking for traces of the Elements.

A long and arduous journey it is, over many days and nights,
Until at last the Elemental Emblem appears, deep within a volcano.

Blazing fire answers the maiden's call,
And the radiance of sacred flames envelops the earth.

13.Title: Belinda - Spark of Hope: Sacred Dawn
13.Content:
"Have you made your mind up, Belinda?"
    In a lava-filled cave deep within the volcanic wasteland of the western Lightbearer Empire, the Fire Elemental Guardian asks the young woman for her final answer.
    Belinda raises her head, exhaustion written on her fair face. Her features are blackened with ash, while her pure white dress is singed and charred by the oppressive heat. Her journey in search of the Fire Guardian had been long and torturous, but her arrival here does not signify an end to her ordeal. The choice she now faced could very well make things even harder, but her steady eyes shone bright with determination:
    "You are not the first to ask me this. Moreover, I've known the answer for a very long time already."
 
 
    A dozen days previously, Belinda had walked hesitantly around the cloisters of the temple, Bishop Palmer's questions still ringing in her ears.
    "Have you made your mind up, Belinda?"
    The peace of the Lightbearer Empire had recently been shattered, when monsters known as Corruptors suddenly appeared in every corner of the land. Even General Rayne had been injured, slipping into a coma from which she could not be awakened. Belinda had tried nonetheless, only to find that the healing power of the Light had no effect on Estrilda or other comatose patients. To make matters worse, the frequency of Corruptor incursions was increasing, with ever more civilians falling before their foul talons. The Temple of Light, always before a place of healing, was now powerless in the face of the comas wrought by Corruptors.
    A spark of hope soon flared, however. The next time Belinda visited Rayne Manor to see how Estrilda fared, a letter from the housekeeper Thane explained the cause behind the current disaster: a catastrophic elemental imbalance, which could only be rectified by finding the five Elemental Guardians.
    She raced back to the Temple and told all this to her mentor, Bishop Palmer. She hoped they might dispatch someone to help scour the volcanic west of the Empire for the Fire Guardian. But Palmer did not immediately grant her request, instead asking if she was sure about her plan, and encouraging her to look deep within herself.
    Belinda understood the Temple's misgivings. To seek salvation anywhere other than the Light would, in the eyes of the laity, be tantamount to admitting the Light's impotence. Insisting on seeking out the Elemental Guardian would also be seen as heresy, and she would be branded an apostate. Distraught, she wondered what else she could do if the Temple refused to help. Suddenly, without even realizing it, she found herself before the door to the Temple, where a commotion brought her back to the present.
    There was a crowd of those afflicted by the disaster, their clothes torn and shabby. Some still clutched small children in their arms as the sisters and brothers of the clergy went among them, handing out bread. When Belinda approached, they noticed her clerical apparel and surged towards her, fervent hope filling their tired eyes.
    A young mother held her child up in front of Belinda, another young victim of the Corruptors. Sadly, this was all too common these days. Belinda knew that the Light had no effect on the afflictions caused by the Corruptors, but also knew that she could not sit idly by as mothers like this looked at her as if she was their final hope.
    Belinda stretched out her hands, letting the Light envelop the child's body. But nothing happened, just like the many other times she had tried and failed.
    The mother fell to her knees, sobbing, as the hope faded from her eyes. Her tears carved two shining paths as they cut through the grime that coated her face: "Is it... Is it because we are not devout enough? I'll dedicate the rest of my life to the Light just please, I beg you... Save my child..." Behind her were countless others, whose gaze swept by the kneeling woman to fall on Belinda.
    She couldn't bear the hope and helplessness in the eyes of the supplicants and made up her mind there and then. There could be no more delay. The Elemental Guardian must be found, and the root cause of this crisis put right.
    "The Light shall protect you."
    Belinda bowed slightly to the despairing crowd, then turned and walked back to the Temple.
 
 
    She burst into his study to find Bishop Palmer sitting with his head in one hand, the other on the desk. He appeared to be examining some important documents.
    "I ask you to let me go to the volcano and find the Elemental Guardian." Belinda broke the silence first. "The elemental imbalance is destroying Esperia's peace. As the priestess of the Temple, I am responsible for thousands of the Empire's citizens."
    Palmer didn't raise his head, but continued staring at the documents before him: "The Light will protect this land, as always."
    "The Light... is not omnipotent."
    Palmer finally looked up, his tone grave as he spoke: "You're treading on dangerous ground, priestess."
    Belinda took a deep breath, aware that she had never before known so clearly what she was going to do. Determined, she speaks resolutely to Palmer: "The elemental chaos must be traced back to its source, and I'm sure the Light will tolerate our pressing need to save people. Please, Bishop, allow me to go at once."
    "The Temple has its own ways to save people. Remember your vows to the Light, priestess."
    "I'm living up to those vows right now." Belinda took a step forward and stood right in front of the desk, looking the Bishop square in the eye, "By the Light above, I will return with hope!"
    Palmer was silent. Ignoring Belinda, he got up without a word and left the study, leaving on his desk what appeared to be an old map. A route was traced on the map, a route which led to the legendary volcano.
    "The Light has always shown me the way," Belinda murmured to herself as she looked towards where Palmer had left. Then, grasping the map tightly, she set out on her journey to the volcano.
 
 
    In the searing heat of the volcano, the Fire Guardian watches the young woman carefully. He saw her perseverance and her faith, but inheriting the Elemental Emblem meant responsibility, and a high price for it: to become the target of the Corruptors, chased endlessly. It was not a decision to be taken lightly.
    "The Light has already written the answer in my heart." Facing the figure in the flames, Belinda seemed to be answering her mentor. "The instant I was ordained, I swore to the Light that I would devote my whole being to my calling, and never abandon anyone who could be saved!"
    The Fire Guardian nodded. "Then it shall be as you wish."
    A mystical rune landed in Belinda's palm, which suddenly burst into violent, surging flames and merged with the pure light that emanated from her. The sacred, golden flames enveloped her, making her seem like a blazing torch that dispelled the darkness and illuminated the dawn. Her hand emerged from the fire, grasping a newly transformed staff.
    The power to save souls was now hers, and she would return bearing renewed hope.

14.Title: Final Chapter: The Solaran Reckoning
14.Content:
The elements ran rampant across Esperia,
Plunging the world into chaos.

As the inheritors of the Emblems gathered in the Bastion of the Elements,
A sinister, long-simmering plot came to light.

Dark chains bound the divine avian in the heart of the volcano.
Casting off her disguise,
The scholar revealed her true, Hypogean colors.

Breaking free of her chains, the divine avian charged towards her captor.
Savage flames lit the cavern, both holy and demonic.

Black feathers floated down like cinders...
The Hypogean's evil had been purified by the flames of the divine.

Thus did celestial radiance reach every corner of the land,
Dispelling the darkness and bringing an end to the Elemental Strife.

15.Title: Maetria - Duskfeather
15.Content:
"When darkness covers the world, the divine avians shall become the fiery salvation of all living things." Such are the great legends regarding the mythical "Obsidian Finches," a species only recorded in the most ancient of histories but which nonetheless once soared high above the skies of Esperia.
 
    It was in that ancient era that Maetria was born. From the time she first opened her eyes in her mother's nest, she had always held fast to the sacred mission told to her again and again by the eldest of the Obsidian Finches. Their sacred duty—the reason for their whole existence—was to protect Esperia.
 
    By the time of the great Elemental Strife that engulfed Esperia, Maetria's dedication to the mission of her race saw her rise to the position of chief over her people. She remembered keenly the words of her ancestors, and leapt into action to save the mortals scurrying fearfully about under their watchful eye. It was her burden, her duty, her honor, to play the role of savior.
 
    The Elemental Strife brought total calamity upon the helpless citizens of a frightened world. But it was nothing unexpected to Maetria and her folk. It was time for their mission to be fulfilled.
 
    Maetria honored all the old precepts taught to her and traveled deep into the Solaran Furnace. There, without reservation, she released the Solaris Flare that dwelled inside her. The ritual had begun. The burning Solaris Flare pierced the ground and lit up the sky in a magnificent display of celestial power, spreading across Esperia and cleansing it of all elemental disorder. Though Maetria felt the power being stripped from her body, she did not then lament the loss of her life, her mind filled only with joy at the glorious fulfilment of her mission. But this pride did not last long. She began to notice a new phenomenon; first with terror, then horror, and finally anger.
 
    She saw all her kinsfolk, all of the other Obsidian Finches, some of whom she had grown up with in the same nest, fall from the sky as the divine Solaris Flare within their bodies was ripped away. She watched them groan on the earth, dying, their feathers fading from brilliant red to gray and then finally ash as the life drained from their bodies. One hatchling Maetria knew well tried desperately to fly over for help. She was already a heap of ash by the time she landed at Maetria's feet.
 
    Maetria had been proud to do her part to save the world—the mission entrusted to her since birth. Yet no one had ever told her that saving the world would also come at the cost of her entire race.
 
    Maetria drew upon all the divine energy within her to try to halt the ritual, but there was nothing she could do. Virtually every member of her race was already dead or dying. Most cried out in pain as they faded to ash in front of her eyes. Maetria also sensed her own life force fading. It was then she came to the cruel realization that, in the end, all of the fanciful-sounding phrases about doing "what is best for Esperia" were nothing more than hollow lies to enable her species' exploitation. No! She resolved to herself. She would not give herself up in sacrifice, she would not die here! She vowed revenge on the world that had cruelly taken her kinsfolk away.
 
    Maetria's anger and desperate desire to save her species called out through the void to sinister forces like a beacon. Fell Hypogeans proffered a deal that Maetria quickly accepted: become their infernal vessel in exchange for unimaginable power. With the power to cheat death, she would live, and as long as she lived there was a hope of restoring her race, of reawakening them from the ash. She would stop at nothing to do so. Soon she emerged from the ash of her dying existence covered in dark flames— Hypogean flames.
 
    Maetria lay in wait for centuries, seeking some means by which the Obsidian Finches could be restored to life. And so passed a thousand years of futile searching, until finally she found the truth about her species' creation, as well as a way forward.
 
    Honas, the God of Creation, crafted the Furnace in the void when he made the world. From the sun he plucked a spark—called the "Solaris Flare"—and mixed it with the elemental forces to create Esperia. Yet a dark force of cosmic chaos had interfered with his great work. Hence, Esperia from its very inception possessed a slight imbalance between the elements, which would eventually culminate in disaster. It was a great defect in Honas' work, but he had a solution. He embedded his Furnace within the planet, in a place virtually undiscoverable. This became the "Solaran Furnace."
 
    Within the Furnace, Honas hid a special stone. Over the centuries, the stone would absorb the Solaran power and give birth to a race of divine avians—the Obsidian Finches.
 
    Eventually the disorder in Esperia's elemental forces culminated in the cataclysm once foretold. It was the Obsidian Finches, the carriers of the Solaris Flare, who were tasked with recreating the world without the imperfections in Honas' original work. Within the Furnace, the Obsidian Finches would have to release the Solaris Flare within themselves, allowing its divine power to spread across the land, seas, and skies. As the essence of their being, removing the Flare from the divine avians would result in their deaths. To protect Esperia with the Solaris Flare would be the glorious burden they would have to bear; yet to Maetria it seemed more a criminal's sentence. The Obsidian Finches were, in the end, no more than tools for correcting the Creator's mistakes, victims of his deceit. They were kindling to be burned.
 
    In this terrible truth, however, Maetria also uncovered a possible means to revive her kinfolk. There was still one Obsidian Finch left, and were the Elemental Strife to strike once more, she would only have to lead this last Finch to the Solaran Furnace. Using the remnants of the Solaris Flare within the last Finch, she could reignite the dormant Furnace and give her people a chance at rebirth.
 
    Maetria waited until a new Strife afflicted Esperia. Talene, the last Obsidian Finch, had made herself known, and within her dwelled the last vestiges of the Solaris Flare. By now, Maetria had waited for millennia, but the time had come for her plans to finally bear fruit. Taking on the guise of a Wilder scholar, she appeared before Talene when the time was right.
 
    "Honored Obsidian Finch, let me tell you a story of the divine avians of old..."

16.Title: Blade of Conviction: Chapter 1
16.Content:
In the solemn and sacred temple,
mortals in misery are seeking their final refuge,
while the hunters have broken the peace here.
The trembling folk recognizes her face—
She's Dura's child, but merciless!
She never lets go of anyone to do with the Hypogeans!
Quivering, the people watch as she approaches.
Neither yelling nor crying can stop her surging will to kill.
Under the Divine Light,
her blade slashes through the sacred temple...

17.Title: Blade of Conviction: Chapter 2
17.Content:
Having been separated from her mother, a girl sought help from the Goddess of Punishment.
The aloof Goddess did not answer the girl's prayers,
Yet still intervened to save her in the moment of her dire need.
The girl followed the Goddess and reunited with her mother.
As a gift of gratitude, she presented a ragdoll she made herself,
Only to have the Goddess turn away and leave silently…
It is said that the Goddess of Punishment never responds mortals' prayers.
But the truth may not be as clear-cut as that.

18.Title: Blade of Conviction: Chapter 3
18.Content:
The Hypogean emerged from his disguise, and the Blade knew it.
He was a long-time quarry of the Goddess.
A few days prior, the Hypogean attacked a camp,
leaving none but a ragged doll in its ruins…
The Hypogean's ceaseless provocation ignited the Goddess' fury.
Under the Divine Light, the Goddess transformed into a giant sword descending from the heavens!
As divine punishment befell, the Hypogean dissipated in its light.
The Goddess returned the doll and left quietly.
Her faith would no longer waver.
She is the sword of judgment that will punish all evil,
always en-route to the next battlefield.

19.Title: Safiya - Maestro of Power
19.Content:
The Queen, ousted by the rebels,
has reclaimed her throne with her allies' help.
But when she ruled her clan again,
her former allies became her greatest threat.
Pacts built upon power are fragile.
The balance between Queens trembles.
When an unknown meteor fell to the ground,
the allies began revealing their intentions.
In this game of power and desire,
only one can last till the end.

20.Title: Eugene's Journal
20.Content:
I seriously cannot believe my bad luck today! I've just been manhandled by the most obstinate Celestial I've ever had the misfortune of talking to. Although I suppose I am fortunate he did not seek to kill me, only to declare—very insistently, I might add—that my supposed Hypogean companion has stolen two very important ancient weapons of his, and I am to be the one to show him how to get them back. 
    Ancient weapons? What on earth is he talking about!? I work alone. I would not, and have never, taken on fellow Hypogean into my confidence. But this Celestial is nothing if not stubborn. He will hear naught of what I have to say on the matter. His only wish is to prevent me from escaping until I can somehow give him what he wants. In other words, I'm now under the effects of a peculiar spell and have been kidnapped!
    I swear I, Eugene, have never been so insulted in my life...

    It won't take us long to chase down the offending Hypogean stuck in the Celestial's bad books. Figures. Now comes the delicate matter of how the brain-dead Celestial "Pigeonhead" is going to handle my release. Is he a Celestial of his word?
    So what explains my new favorite moniker for this fool: "Pigeonhead"? Because he lacks manners. Because I keep asking him his name and he keeps refusing to answer. Because I have no choice but to go with the option that most closely resembles his defects?
    Then again, I've always used nicknames for their kind since they all seem to be afflicted with those deformed pigeon wings of theirs.

    When we finally closed in on that Hypogean, ol' Pigeonhead was quite the eager beaver. I was happy to follow a plan. Not him. He bolted after the darned thing and... who do I talk to get a new partner?
    Pigeonhead bit off more than he could chew. My alleged Hypogean partner does have a partner, it seems—many partners, just not me. And so, without further ado, we were on the brink of a cliff and had a very ungraceful descent. One I hadn't had the misfortune of enduring before. The entire trip would've been such a tremendous waste if I hadn't had the foresight to grab that chest of weapons from our enemies' hands at the very last second.

    The dreadful thought has occurred to me that my Pigeonhead companion may not be the great Celestial he claims to be, but a child trafficker! What else am I to do with the fact that the "ancient weapons" are no artifacts at all, but two little demon children still very much in the milk-drinking phase.
    Yet this should not concern me in the slightest. I've already fulfilled my side of the bargain. He got what he wanted. Won't he keep his word and let me go free? Apparently "things are more complicated than I'd realized". What's that supposed to mean? Then he told me a magical device for breaking my curse is broken! In other words, he has a very good reason for keeping me captive a while longer...
    But all of this is academic if I can't find a way out of this demon place. Right, more bad luck. Particularly, the bad luck of jumping out of a frying pan and into a fire or, rather, off a cliff into a network of terrible underground caverns that lead you in circles. And would you believe it? It is in this august place several dragons have decided to make their home!

    It has struck me as distinctly possible that I might have become the very first Hypogean nanny in all of history, which is not a role I have exactly trained for. One of the little naughty brats has a habit of pulling my hair, finding it amusing beyond what any sane creature would think. I keep asking myself: who exactly is the real Hypogean here?
    The baby boy is quite the obedient one, all full of smiles for me. So wonderfully ignorant of the world... Although I have to give him some credit: he is adorable.
    In his infinite wisdom, Pigeonhead the Celestial has decided to put me in charge of the two little brats just in case they ran into some kind of danger. Where I'm from our young are not used to being cuddled in this way. They can't be that delicate?!
    Although normally rather quiet Pigeonhead becomes quite animated whenever I bring up this issue of letting the young'uns exert a greater degree of freedom. I don't have the patience to endure his long spiels.
    No, I need to get away from this madman!

    We lifted the curse! Well done to us, me in particular. Now I can say goodbye to Pigeonhead and his ankle-biters. A few more days of having my hair pulled out by that energetic demon child and I'm going to have to embrace baldness—not the style I was hoping for at this particular moment in my life.
    Gavus even had the temerity to thank me. I don't know what the world is coming to when a Celestial feels himself greatly indebted to a Hypogean? Amazing one of heaven's ugly faces can say that.
    By the way, I finally did figure out Pigeonhead's real name: Gavus. This, of course, he revealed as I was about to walk out of their lives forever. I think I'll stick to Pigeonhead. Of course, that also implies I will never meet him again, which is not likely if I have anything to say about it.

    I've had a few days now to appreciate my glorious freedom, yet my thoughts keep turning back to the fate of Gavus and the little devils.
    It's strange not to be kept up until late at night by screeching... It almost feels as if the wee hours of the morning are missing something? I wonder if the little girl is still trying to destroy her surroundings? Or have the experiences of the last few days mellowed her? It also concerns me that Gavus, while not completely incompetent, may not be up to the challenge of caring for children. Let's just say that any mother that left them to his care would be something less than responsible.
    Darnit! I'm a Hypogean! I need to be thinking Hypogean thoughts! What are these filthy... pangs of conscience?
    But would it be so bad to... visit them after all this time? If only for a few minutes. I shall leave now. There's no harm in it...

    I turned up a little late. My Hypogean cousins do not share my ambivalence toward Pigeonhead and his cursed kids. I arrive to discover he and the children were attacked moments prior, the little ones badly injured.
    Pigeonhead was trying to channel his energies into a healing salve, an endeavor in which I assisted. I can't say it was very effective, but their condition will not worsen for the time being. I feel the experience has wounded Pigeonhead emotionally too. His face has sunk into solid worry as he keeps trying, again and again, to use what little magic he has left to heal the children fully.
    Then when I see Pigeonhead almost fully drain himself of all magicks in his futile quest to heal the children, he turns to me and says: "There may be another way."

    Pigeonhead is mad. He keeps talking to me about finding some "Cradle of Truth" which will allow him to call on his fellow Celestials and then, presumably, all will be well for the children. 
    The little girl spent some time awake today to play with my hair for a few minutes before returning to her deep slumber. The difference is quite noticeable. She is wasting away, her strength fading. I took her hand in mine to help her pull...
    The little ones are vulnerable. I can see Pigeonhead was not exaggerating.
    I suspect Pigeonhead is overextending himself in his healing. Magical exhaustion is not a pleasant prospect. He wouldn't be able to carry on...

    We finally made it out of that hellhole. And when dawn comes Pigeonhead has claimed his fellow Celestials will meet us here, and then the safety of the two young'uns will be assured.
    I think Pigeonhead is grasping at straws. What makes him think his kind will heal two naughty babies? He may have his agenda, but something tells me the Celestials are more inclined to strike first and ask questions later. He's so naive. And won't hear a word of it.
    We're only hours from when my misgivings will be confirmed or denied, and Pigeonhead may be forced to choose between his conscience and the people. I have no desire to fight another battle.
    I hope I'm very much mistaken...

21.Title: The Metallurgist's Diary
21.Content:
Today is the day of our great Guardian, Gaius, declared war on the Celestials!
    What a moment for the ages: when mankind finally turned away from the Heavens to stand upon our own two feet and declare ourselves the masters of our fate!
    What more does mankind need to prove that we are more than equal to the Celestials? Our buildings already tower into the skies and compare with the highest peaks. Skyscraping airships brush against the upper atmosphere and the shoulders of the Celestials' Palaces already.
    Our civilization, its embrace of magical strength, has reached a pinnacle from which mankind can work the greatest miracles! The Celestials should be the ones kneeling to us, not us to them.
    Dearest and most venerable Guardian, I salute you as humanity's envoy and representative of our combined glory and honor. I pledge myself to your service as I should—and everyone ought!
    I've heard the Dean is currently selecting students from the Academy for a personal audience with our mighty leader. As a faithful devotee of your way and your mighty works, I look forward to the incredible day when I can lay eyes on you, your lowliest servant. I look forward to the day I can contribute my blood, sweat, and tears to your cause—sword of your strength, shield of your valor, ready to lay waste to the mountains of the gods!

    The Dean just took me for an audience with Guardian!
    I had the privilege to overhear our great Guardian's army is facing some difficulties, and so the decision has been made to reduce the minimum age of enlistment by two years. This has upset some of the conscripts in the southern provinces.
    To the reason for our audience with the mighty Guardian. As Chief Astral Mage in the court, our Dean's opinions carry great weight, and he has been advising on the creation of a powerful new artifact using our mastery over the magical energies of the sun and moon. It is to be the most powerful weapon of all time, capable of crushing continents or breaking the sky into pieces. A weapon, in other words, capable of ending this war. Who but our Dean, the most accomplished of human sorcerers, could be commissioned for this project? I and the other students shall serve as his right-hand researchers. And so we begin its construction!
    My mind races with thoughts of my august future given that, at my age, I've already been in the physical presence of our great Guardian! I realize now that history has selected me to be one of its key contributors. And I do believe and have every confidence that my prodigious abilities in metallurgy and alchemy will help forge this amazing weapon.

    We've already crafted two prototypes of the weapon our Dean sketched out, one named "Dawn" and the other "Dusk". But live demonstrations revealed a destructive power far less than what our great leader had envisioned.
    As I have said before, this result is not unexpected given our Dean's overly conservative methodology. It can't be deployed at full strength of magical.
    If only my co-contributor had the sense to adopt my plan—combining bio-alchemy with the original design—he would find solutions magic alone cannot. His response? "As long as I'm here, you can forget about polluting my lab with your immoral ideas!" This a foolish reply from tired moralizers with nothing to contribute but old ideas.
    It is the most ridiculous situation imaginable, and yet here I am putting it to paper. Here we have a researcher who knows the way forward, whose ideas might hold the key to the weapon's full potential, who is now to be shut down with questions of ethics?!
    I can already tell what will happen if the research team does not change track soon. So there is no point waiting for the outcome. I've already begun my own secret experiments. Bio-alchemy has been rejected by the mainstream for far too long out of a malformed fear that some great disaster will take place upon tampering with the human spirit. It is a fear not borne by any evidence.
    People fear simply what they do not know. That is natural. But I have seen the results firsthand. It should not be a source of dread, but recognized as an untapped source of blessings! Once those blessings are revealed, I shall be thoroughly vindicated and my critics condemned.

    Today marks the seventh in what is shaping up to be a long week of experiments which have not, I must sadly write, gone as well as I'd expected. It may be a question of size. I suspect younger subjects may be needed...
    New organic entities require an old organic for fuel. It is a sacrifice, yes, but one eminently necessary for the future of human civilization.
    I'm sensing very strongly that I am on the brink of some amazing discovery sure to cement my name on history's page. I need only persist a little longer. I'll be able to present my innovative results directly to the great Guardian himself!
    My newest test subjects should be arriving any moment. And I haven't a moment to waste!

    Guardian is getting impatient with the misguided efforts of my Dean, just as I'd expected. He toured the laboratory just a few days ago, loudly noting the weapon's power is far from what's required. It seems he is considering scrapping the entire project.
    What wonderful news!
    The time has come for my doubts about Dean's approach shall be utterly vindicated! My newest experiments have been proceeding extraordinarily well, with the latest attachments to my subjects provoking a robust, heightened Invigorating Essence. Even more positively, the bodies of these hybrids showed no sign of rejecting my implants!
    It is essentially a demonstration of the correctness of my approach: the only weapon that can turn the tide of this war is to be found in bio-alchemy.
    I've arranged an audience with Guardian in just three days. I'm almost giddy with thoughts of the glory and prestige I'm about to win for myself in this brave new field of discovery!

    I can do nothing if not commemorate this day.
    I demonstrated beyond all reasonable doubt to the Guardian the success and viability of my approach, and untapped promises of bio-alchemy. But my dumb old Dean—had the gall to criticize my every decision in front of Guardian himself! He even had the temerity to call my efforts a "disgusting disgrace" to the Academy and repudiation of every ethical boundary ever instituted! I can't believe someone from our Academy just threatened the leader of our people with resignation!
    Guardian abruptly lifted his sword and cleaved his head from his neck. He then pointed straight at me and declared: "Your turn!"
    It's hard to accurately convey the joy and vindication I felt at that moment. My poor old teacher, if only you had come to your senses earlier. We could have worked together! Instead, you had to doubt Guardian's plans and authority—and even threaten the man himself!
    From this moment on I shall be assuming full control of the project, which I'm very determined to lead into a new and exciting era!

    We have commenced bio-alchemy trials with plenty of subjects on a real scale, and also taken many steps to integrate it with the original weapons. We're making real progress for the first time in ages. The first bio-alchemic weapons test failed, but this was not unanticipated. In a way, it confirms another hypothesis: only by endowing real intelligence into "Dusk" and "Dawn" shall we be able to wield its full strength and turn this war in our favor!
    I must rectify immediately with the construction of an enormous energy field that should provide an ongoing power supply. I have nicknamed it the "Cradle of Truth", symbolically as the weapons mark our emergence from a cradle of vulnerability to a Celestial plane of strength where we are equal to the gods. It's declaration enough to the world that our power is in no way inferior to the output of the sun!
    Of course, not everything can go as planned in such a grand scheme.
    The old Dean had his supporters. I can't be sure whether they are deliberately trying to undermine the project by offering stupid suggestions, or simply too dumb to realize its potential. Their attitudes bother me, particularly after my new ranking. If they don't want to support me with useful ideas, then at least they can get their hands dirty at the coalface of the industry—the difficult construction of the Cradle of Truth. But I'll make sure that the firing mechanism can only be exercised by my hand alone.
    There is much to anticipate in the coming weeks: humanity's ascendancy into a new era.

    As I'd very much expected, with some disgruntled former classmates who idolized the old Dean and don't like getting their hands dirty on the Cradle of Truth's construction. Gossiping about my "unclean methods", whatever that means? They're extremely envious of my success and that I had them taken out of their cozy lab. For all I know, they're probably planning to destroy the Cradle in the final moments of its construction.
    Heh! The very thought that this project could have ever succeeded with people of that caliber seems laughable. It's time we took a page out of the Guardian's book when it comes to disobedient researchers...
    I try not to let such trivialities affect my mood. Recent trials to integrate consciousness into the weapons are going well. We just need to stay the course and all of our efforts will be rewarded with a masterpiece.
    The very last thing I can do would be to never disappoint our great Guardian and the hopes of humanity. And the worst thing I can do is to allow some fools to endanger this vitally important project.

    Experiments, experiments, experiments! I've almost lost track of the number of subjects that have passed through these halls.
    I was quite disturbed when I woke up today to receive a very unfortunate update, an update that will forever sear this day with infamy. I have been told our great Guardian himself perished on the front lines while fighting on behalf of all humanity! A cold chill swept through my bones as I realized just how cruel and capricious the Celestials can be. They must be celebrating.
    I've ordered the news be kept secret from all the others here. Let no one breathe a word of it! It will be better for everyone's resolve if the memory of our Guardian is kept blameless, pure, and alive as an invincible warrior on the field whose singular vision is guaranteed to save humanity. I will not let their minds be troubled. His will still live in us—to recover humanity's place in the cosmos.
    And indeed the completion of the project nears at a rapid pace as we put the finishing touches on the new and improved weapons. It'll be our chance to wipe the smiles off those arrogant Celestials.
    The Celestials shall be cast down into the mud as the true masters and commanders of Esperia, humanity, shall go on to achieve greater and greater heights of glory!

    Heh! Success! The weapons have been successfully modified into a far more powerful state!
    We've achieved a perfect symbiotic union between experimental subject 637 and Dusk. A similar successful result with Dawn should see the project move well and truly beyond the development phase into a more mature frame.
    It is a magnificent thing we have accomplished at the lab today, a miracle of human ingenuity by which we shall achieve miracles for humanity in this war.
    When I look at the little weapons, they remind me of nothing so much as two poor babies who nonetheless have the potential inside to rise and destroy even the gods. And I'll be right there when they do, bearing witness to a delicious spectacle of Celestials crushed under our feet.
    Heh! What can the pathetic Celestials do to us now? It is our time to dominate the world!

    A messenger from the front has just delivered more bad news. I've just been told a strike team of Celestials is headed here.
    Someone must have leaked word of the project! I would have thought that for the sake of humanity, people could keep their mouths shut, but no. It is especially troubling when I consider Guardian took great care to execute everyone not working directly inside the facility who knew about its existence. Did someone overhear something who survive to tell the tale? A fish slipped the net? Well done, traitor of humanity. Yet I can guess the Celestials still don't realize the project's true potential. If they did, their entire army would be on their way.
    Unfortunately, this has dramatically cut our preparation time. There are just too many things we need to do to wrap this up. All the threads of this project must now be pursued simultaneously.
    The news has also removed the last shreds of guilt I felt for my disgruntled ex-research colleagues whose lives I had to expend on the more difficult aspects of the project's development. But I should have been more efficient in destroying evidence of our existence.
    I can only rest once the weapon has been connected to a secure power source and activated. More time would have been nice, but time is a luxury and, besides, I'd love to see the expressions on their face when the Celestials get to experience our weapon firsthand.

    Curses! The Celestial attack came far earlier than I'd anticipated. We lost control of the Cradle of Truth! And this stronghold is also in danger. The energy supply is only half completed, and neither of the weapons could be activated. And there's nothing I can do about it.
    No! This was my life, my blood, my handiwork! I'd rather have everything destroyed than see them walk away with my accomplishment!
    I've hidden in the weapons in a place they'll never find! But I must take additional steps to ensure they never discover exactly what we have been working on. Hah! Because they know as long as rumors of this weapon abound, as long as it might potentially exist, they are still in danger and humanity is always on the brink of a comeback.
    Curse you, Celestials! From the depths of Hades, I do curse thee! Savor your victory. Because your Judgment Day is coming. And when it comes, the glory of humanity shall trample you eternally underfoot!

27.Title: Lyca - The Dawnbringer
27.Content:
As the ominous meteor falls,
Darkness and calamity engulf the Dark Forest.
The Hypogeans trap the lost commander in an illusory realm,
Hell-bent on wearing her will thin and occupying her body.
Yet her bond with her comrades
Lets her see clearly the path she is seeking.
No longer relying on the guidance of the stars,
She resolves to transform into a sharp arrow that pierces through the darkness,
Bringing light back to the Dark Forest.

28.Title: Shemira - The Soulreaver
28.Content:
The anguished mother, having lost everything,
Is finally able to stay with her child forever.
But fate has yet another cruel plan in store for her.
When the child's extraordinary talents catch the eyes of the greedy,
When disaster strikes out of the blue,
And when the most dreadful nightmare recurs…
A mother's heart shall remain staunchly resolute.
